output.evidence: Version 1 (image 5) resolves the 'Frosted Glass Dawn Veil' concept as a finished set: the backlit frosted slab reads as a wall with a cool dawn glow blooming behind it, meeting a continuous matte frosted floor along a clean horizon, so the star flacon stands on plausible ground with a soft contact shadow sunk into the grain at its lower point. The right-hand type column is coherent and hierarchical (letter-spaced 'Mugler' cap, large narrow sans 'Angel', frost-blue rule beneath), sitting beside the bottle and overlapping its shoulder band vertically while staying wide-separated horizontally, exactly per the brief's beside relation. Version 2 (image 6) loses the architectural frosted wall: the glow drifts to the top edge instead of behind the sheet, and the ground becomes a convex dome horizon that reads as a raised podium edge behind the packshot, weakening the continuous wall-to-floor material and making the bottle's contact ambiguous. Both keep the product faithful (opaque silver wedge cap, lavender-to-ice translucent star), but version 1's controlled materials, believable ground plane and quieter negative space make it the stronger finished poster.
